                                       PROJECT NO. 58481
 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                            §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION §                       §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                      §                   OF TEXAS



                     COMMENTS OF THE DOW CHEMICAL COMPANY

                                         I.    COMMENTS

       The Dow Chemical Company (Dow) submits these comments to address new proposed
§25.194(l) in the recent draft rule, which provides as follows:

       (l)     ERCOT operational standards.

               (1)     ERCOT may establish operational standards for large load customers to
                       ensure system reliability.

               (2)     A large load customer must comply with operational standards, developed
                       through ERCOT protocols, as a condition for interconnection and continued
                       operation of the customer’s load.

At Dow, we’re passionate about using the power of materials science to make a real difference in
the world. As one of the leading companies in our field, we work every day to deliver innovative,
sustainable solutions that help address challenges in packaging, infrastructure, mobility, and
consumer applications. Here in Texas, Dow operates nine manufacturing sites, a business center,
and an R&D hub—making us the largest materials science company in the state. Our Texas
Operations in Freeport, 85 years strong, is the largest integrated chemical complex in the Western
Hemisphere, spanning 20 square miles and producing nearly 30% of Dow’s U.S. products. Across
Texas, we employ more than 6,700 people and partner with 4,000 contractors, contributing $1.2
billion in payroll and benefits, $640 million in local purchases, and over $189 million in taxes
annually. Dow has been operating in ERCOT for decades and there has never been a need to
control our operations for reliability purposes.

Industrial facilities are not “one-size fits all.” Different industries and even different sites within
the same industry have very different operating characteristics. Within Dow’s industrial sites alone
we have some sites with less than 100 MW and others with closer to 800 MW of total peak demand.
Some of our sites have behind the meter generation and are merely balanced using grid purchases
or sales while others rely solely on the grid for reliable electricity supply. In most cases we have
multiple production units, producing multiple end use products, using multiple technologies
behind each site’s grid interconnection. ERCOT is not suited to impose operational restrictions on
these businesses, which, although they may have some power production capabilities, are not in
the utility or generation business.

                                                    1
 Ensuring process safety is the most important aspect of running our operations. Mandating that
industrial sites operate under electric grid conditions for which their equipment was not
originally designed may lead to significant health, safety, and environmental risks for our
employees and the surrounding communities. We believe that ERCOT may not have the
specialized expertise required to address the complex process safety considerations that could
result from these circumstances.

Disconnecting industrial manufacturing loads because they cannot comply with operational
standards imposed by ERCOT and intended primarily to address issues caused by other industries
is not reasonable and will compromise key sectors that contribute to the state’s economy.

Over the last eight plus decades, Dow has invested billions of dollars into manufacturing
equipment, infrastructure, jobs, and the Texas economy. A significant part of why Dow has been
able to make these investment decisions into Texas, for operations that are not short term but
instead operate for several decades, is the regulatory certainty that Texas has provided. This has
culminated in the “Texas Miracle” which has made Texas so prosperous. These potential
operational standards that would be imposed by ERCOT would be in direct conflict with that
regulatory certainty required to make long-term investment decisions. While we understand the
need to have increased control and certainty on new developing industries, operations like ours
have been in place for several decades without issue. We have significant concern with the impact
that this proposal could have going forward and respectfully request that the proposal be revised.




                                            Respectfully submitted,

                                            The Dow Chemical Company




                                            Kreshka Young, North America Business Director
                                            2154 Enclave Parkway, Houston, TX 77450
                                            kyoung2@dow.com
                                            832-674-6719
